record.title: 22 x 16 x 4 deep-groove ball bearing, Ø16.0000 bore / Ø22.0000 OD / 4.0000 wide — bought (MR1622-ZZ), the ring Pollen's own mesh carries
record.why: MEASURED 2026-09-02 (lane T): the folder's previous words, 'created by `bin/triad new part` — nothing measured yet', were already false and are replaced. cad/interfaces.json now declares two MEASURED anchors, 'bore' and 'od', read off seeed_bearing__configuration__22x16x4.stl by cecad.meshfeatures.cylinders — Ø16.0000 bore / Ø22.0000 OD / 4.0000 wide, every fit at 0.0000 mm residual and 355.0 deg cover, frozen in out/laneT/features/seeed_bearing__configuration__22x16x4.json; cad/part.py builds the envelope from the same numbers; sourcing.json carries verified offers under MPN MR1622-ZZ. WHAT KEEPS IT AT CANNOT DETERMINE, named: (1) the folder's own build has NOT been run to completion — `ce-cad/bin/cad tools/build_mesh_loaders.py bearing-22x16x4` was started on 2026-09-02 at 22:57 and had burned 131 minutes of CPU over 3 h 43 min of wall clock without finishing, on a machine at 1-minute load 41-80 from other lanes' FreeCAD jobs; until it returns, whether this folder produces one valid solid is unmeasured. (2) NO STANDARD IS CLAIMED: a 10x15x3 deep-groove ball bearing looks like an ISO 15 boundary-dimension part and this folder does NOT assert that, because nobody here has checked the series against ISO 15 — asserting it would earn a T4 tier on a guess. What settles that: read ISO 15's dimension table for the 6700 series and record it in record.standard, or drop the claim for good.
record.origin_why: a BOUGHT part. sourcing.json carries verified distributor offers under MPN MR1622-ZZ (record.verdict PASS); the geometry in cad/part.py is a datasheet-faithful envelope of Pollen's published mesh reference/pollen-microduck-rl/assets/seeed_bearing__configuration__22x16x4.stl, measured with cecad.meshfeatures.cylinders and cecad.meshslice.intervals and graded against that mesh by cad-refcheck.
